events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Maricopa, AZ; Yuma, AZ

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:21AM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
weather.areaDesc: Maricopa, AZ; Yuma, AZ

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 12 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint

Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal

to 7 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 AM EST Monday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 PM EST this evening. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...High astronomical tides and large surf may cause moderate to major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one half to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon. . * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

location.region: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 21 at 9:57AM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides and large surf may cause moderate
to major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino
Coast. Up to one half to one foot of saltwater inundation above
ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon. .

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above ground level. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County Coast zones. * WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning. While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides early next week.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 1:40PM PST until November 22 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to
2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and
low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation
along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above
ground level.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast
may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning.
While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of
coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides
early next week.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides between about 730 AM and 930 AM. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to high surf is expected much of the week, with even the possibility of warning- level surf at times from Wednesday afternoon into Thursday. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Elevated coastal water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest tide line. * WHERE...Coastal Kuskokwim Delta Communities, including Kipnuk, Kongiganak, and Kwigillingok. * WHEN...3 AM Sunday to 3 AM AKST Monday. * IMPACTS...Elevated coastal water levels driven by southeast winds gusting to 55 mph. Coastal erosion is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Gusty southeasterly winds will begin increasing early Sunday morning as the storm approaches. Highest water levels expected late Sunday night. Winds will diminish by Sunday evening, and seas will subside by Monday morning following the natural high tide cycle.

location.region: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island

weather.description:

* WHERE...Coastal Kuskokwim Delta Communities, including Kipnuk,
Kongiganak, and Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...3 AM Sunday to 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Elevated coastal water levels driven by southeast
winds gusting to 55 mph. Coastal erosion is possible.

events.description: * WHAT...South to southwest winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and steep seas 9 to 12 ft through tonight. For the Gale Watch, from Monday morning through Tuesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are possible.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above ground level. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County Coast zones. * WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning. While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides early next week.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 8:17PM PST until November 22 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to
2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and
low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation
along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above
ground level.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast
may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning.
While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of
coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides
early next week.
weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3- 5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

location.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal

events.description: * WHAT...Up to 2.8 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Pacific Ocean Coast. * WHEN...Through 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. The river may hold steady early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage then forecast mid to late week. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are inaccessible due to knee-deep water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 4.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 4.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is forecast to hold steady near 4.1 feet early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage forecast mid to late week. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river

forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 4.1 feet.

early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage
forecast mid to late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase this upcoming week. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re- breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above ground level. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County Coast zones. * WHEN...From 7 AM this morning to 3 PM PST this afternoon. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning. While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides early next week.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 3:29AM PST until November 22 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:

2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County

* WHEN...From 7 AM this morning to 3 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast
may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning.

coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides
early next week.
weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday night through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two feet above ground level, during high tides is possible along the immediate coast as well as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding of low-lying areas is expected due to high tides. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and property. A Coastal Flood Watch means that more significant coastal flooding due to a combination of high surf and high tides is possible. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to protect property.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides between about 730 AM and 930 AM. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to high surf is expected much of the week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to reach 5.3 feet and Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue a gradual rise through the week. For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Deland. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 2:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 5.3 feet. - Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 2:30 PM EST Sunday was 5.3 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising in Major Flood Stage through the week. - Flood stage is 4.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to
reach 5.3 feet and Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
continue a gradual rise through the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 5.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising in Major
Flood Stage through the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EST.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.
